body:
## What is a commercial lease make-good obligation?

Make-good provisions address obligations relating to the premises at the end of a lease, where applicable. The actual documents and circumstances need review; a generic description does not establish the work your business must perform or its cost.

For a Newcastle or Hunter business, begin with your solicitor's clarification of the lease position, then organise the site information and project inputs needed to plan any agreed work. This is a practical briefing method, not legal advice or a contractor quote.

## Gather the documents before pricing work

Collect the signed lease, amendments, available condition records, plans, approvals and relevant correspondence. Identify which information is missing and who may hold it. Ask your solicitor to explain the provisions and unresolved questions for the actual premises.

**Helpful tip:** keep a document register with revision dates so the solicitor and project team are considering the same information.

## Turn clarified requirements into a work brief

Once the lease questions have been addressed with your solicitor, record the actual work to be assessed, the premises condition and the assumptions requiring confirmation. Ask the appropriate appointed specialists to assess matters within their expertise.

| Brief item | Information to record | Question to resolve |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Documents | Lease references, amendments and condition records | Which obligation or assumption needs clarification? |
| Existing site | Layout, photos, installed items and retained areas | What needs inspection before estimating? |
| Proposed scope | Removal, repair, reinstatement or other identified work | Which activities are included and excluded? |
| Access and timing | Site access, operating limits and confirmed dates | What dependencies affect the sequence? |
| Completion | Required records, inspections and outstanding actions | Who confirms each item and closes it out? |

Do not assume that labels such as cosmetic make-good or full reinstatement establish the same scope in every building. Use an itemised brief for the actual site.

## Build a site-specific budget

Seek appropriately scoped contractor and specialist inputs. Compare quantities, exclusions, allowances, access assumptions, disposal, services interfaces and the GST basis. Record the validity period and information still needed to replace working allowances with firmer estimates.

A generic rate per square metre is not a verified quote for your premises. This guide does not publish market cost ranges or assume a negotiated cap or settlement will be available.

**Helpful tip:** ask providers to price against the same scope revision and list clarifications beside the comparison, rather than judging only the total.

[Use the FitOut budget planning method](/blog/office-fitout-cost-guide-australia-2026)

## Office make-good checklist: five questions before accepting a price

1. **What obligation has been clarified?** Keep the relevant document reference and your solicitor's advice with the brief. An agent's shorthand description is not the complete record.
2. **What physical work is being priced?** List each item, quantity or area, the expected outcome and what is to remain. Have the relevant specialists inspect uncertain conditions.
3. **What does the proposal leave out?** Ask about access, disposal, services interfaces, inspections, completion records, allowances and the GST basis as relevant to the actual scope.
4. **When can the work happen?** Connect the outgoing site with the new site's readiness, furniture removal, IT, building access and any required inspections.
5. **How will closeout be recorded?** Name the person responsible for each outstanding item. Ask your solicitor what written confirmation is appropriate for the actual lease position.

[Download the office make-good scope and handback worksheet (CSV)](/downloads/office-make-good-scope-worksheet.csv). No email is required. Use it to record questions, confirmed scope and evidence; it does not determine your legal obligations or certify completion.

## Example: two prices for different work are not comparable

Imagine two proposals for the same office. One allows for removing selected partitions and repainting affected areas. The other also includes services adjustments, disposal and work outside normal access hours. This is an illustrative comparison, not a client project or a statement of what your lease requires.

Before choosing a price, ask both providers to identify their assumptions against the same brief. Some extra items may be required, some may be unnecessary and some may still need specialist assessment. The total alone does not tell you which is correct.

Keep a simple clarification log: item, document or drawing reference, proposed treatment, person who must advise, price status and decision. Once the scope is clarified, obtain an updated proposal with the agreed inclusions and exclusions. This makes the comparison traceable without pretending the lowest number covers everything.

## Handback evidence: organise it before the last day

A practical handback pack may include the agreed scope revision, relevant photos, contractor records, inspection actions, keys and access reconciliation, and correspondence about unresolved items. Confirm what is appropriate with the appointed team and solicitor for your actual premises.

| Record | Why it helps | Who to confirm it with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Clarified scope and source references | Shows the basis on which work was assessed | Your solicitor and appointed project advisers |
| Dated condition photos | Records the state of identified areas | The party coordinating site records |
| Required completion documents | Collects evidence for the actual work packages | The relevant appointed contractors and advisers |
| Outstanding-action list | Keeps unfinished work and questions visible | Each named action owner |
| Handover correspondence | Records what was communicated and remains unresolved | Your solicitor for the legal effect |

Physical completion, a key return and a legal release are different matters. Have your solicitor advise on the effect of any handover document or proposed settlement rather than assuming one task closes every obligation.

## Connect the outgoing and incoming sites

If the business is relocating, include both sites in the plan. Identify who coordinates removal, technology changeovers, furniture, access and any period when the business needs to operate across locations.

Ask your solicitor to confirm lease dates and requirements. The project team should establish a programme for the actual work and supplier inputs rather than relying on a generic notice window or move timetable.

**Helpful tip:** keep commercial obligations and delivery tasks visible as separate workstreams with named owners.

[Use the office relocation checklist](/blog/office-relocation-checklist)

## Track completion and remaining actions

Agree with the appointed advisers and providers what information, inspections and records are needed for the actual scope. Retain the relevant correspondence, photos and completion documentation, and track unresolved items to an owner.

Have your solicitor advise on any proposed settlement, release or dispute. Do not assume that finishing a physical task settles every lease issue.

**Helpful tip:** maintain an open-action register that continues after the move, with a clear owner for documents and follow-up questions.

## Official guidance and applicability

The NSW Small Business Commissioner discusses make-good provisions and condition records in its leasing guidance. Have your solicitor confirm how the actual lease applies.

The linked NSW retail leasing guidance should not be assumed to apply to every office or industrial lease. Ask your solicitor which requirements apply to your premises and transaction.

[NSW Small Business Commissioner: end of the lease](https://www.smallbusiness.nsw.gov.au/help/common-questions/what-to-do-at-the-end-of-the-lease)

[NSW Small Business Commissioner: leasing costs](https://www.smallbusiness.nsw.gov.au/help/common-questions/understanding-the-costs-of-leasing)

## Office make-good questions

### What does office make-good include?

The scope depends on the actual lease documents, condition records and circumstances. Ask your solicitor to clarify the obligation, then have the appropriate appointed specialists assess the physical work. Do not assume every office needs full reinstatement.

### Can I budget for make-good using a square metre rate?

A generic rate is not a verified quote for your premises. Build a defined scope and compare site-specific contractor inputs, exclusions, access assumptions, allowances and GST basis.

### Is returning the keys enough to close the lease obligations?

Do not assume so. Physical completion, key return and any legal release are separate matters. Your solicitor should advise on the actual requirements and the effect of handover correspondence.

### Can YOS help coordinate an office make-good plan?

YOS can discuss the agreed tenant-side commercial workstream and client-side coordination. Your solicitor provides legal advice and appointed contractors carry out trade and construction work. Responsibilities are scoped before work begins.
